summary: A runnable code repository for the MiniEncoder model, a compact Transformer encoder for binary sentiment classification.

parameters.name: vocab_size
parameters.reason: Size of the vocabulary for the model.

parameters.name: embedding_dim
parameters.reason: Dimension of the embeddings for the model.

parameters.name: num_heads
parameters.reason: Number of attention heads in the Transformer model.

parameters.name: head_dim
parameters.reason: Dimension of each attention head in the model.

parameters.name: dropout_rate
parameters.reason: Dropout rate applied after attention and feed-forward layers.

parameters.name: batch_size
parameters.reason: Batch size for training the model.

files.purpose: Entry point for running the MiniEncoder model training and evaluation.

function_skeletons.name: main
function_skeletons.signature: def main(config_path: str, seed: int) -> None:
function_skeletons.docstring:
Main entry point for the MiniEncoder training and evaluation process. 

Args:
    config_path (str): Path to the configuration file.
    seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility.
core_steps: Parse command line arguments for config and seed.
Load configuration from the specified JSON file.
Set the random seed for reproducibility.
Prepare the dataset using the specified parameters.
Initialize the MiniEncoder model with the configuration settings.
Train the model on the prepared dataset.
Evaluate the model and print the results.

acceptance_criteria: The script runs without errors when provided with valid arguments.
The model trains and evaluates correctly based on the provided configuration.

files.purpose: Configuration file for the MiniEncoder model settings.
acceptance_criteria: The configuration file is valid JSON.
All required parameters are present and have sensible default values.

files.purpose: Data loading and preprocessing for the sentiment classification dataset.

function_skeletons.name: load_data
function_skeletons.docstring:
Load and preprocess the sentiment classification dataset.

Args:
    file_path (str): Path to the dataset file.

Returns:
    Tuple[List[str], List[int]]: A tuple containing the list of texts and their corresponding labels.
core_steps: Read the dataset file from the specified path.
Tokenize the text data into sentences.
Map the text data to token ids based on the vocabulary.
Return the tokenized texts and their labels.

key_variables.name: texts
key_variables.purpose: List of text samples from the dataset.

key_variables.name: labels
key_variables.purpose: List of corresponding labels for the text samples.

acceptance_criteria: The function loads the dataset correctly and returns the expected format.
The dataset is tokenized and mapped to ids as specified.

files.purpose: Implementation of the MiniEncoder model architecture.

function_skeletons.name: __init__
function_skeletons.signature: def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, embedding_dim: int, num_heads: int, head_dim: int, dropout_rate: float) -> None:
function_skeletons.docstring:
Initialize the MiniEncoder model with the specified parameters.

Args:
    vocab_size (int): Size of the vocabulary.
    embedding_dim (int): Dimension of the embeddings.
    num_heads (int): Number of attention heads.
    head_dim (int): Dimension of each attention head.
    dropout_rate (float): Dropout rate for the model.
core_steps: Set the vocabulary size, embedding dimension, number of heads, head dimension, and dropout rate as instance variables.
Initialize the embedding layer, positional encoding, and Transformer encoder layers.

function_skeletons.name: forward
function_skeletons.docstring:
Forward pass through the MiniEncoder model.

Args:
    x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of token ids.

Returns:
    torch.Tensor: Output logits for classification.
core_steps: Pass the input tensor through the embedding layer.
Add positional encodings to the embeddings.
Apply the Transformer encoder layers to the embeddings.
Pool the output and pass it through the classification head.

acceptance_criteria: The model initializes without errors with valid parameters.
The forward pass produces output of the correct shape.

files.purpose: Training loop for the MiniEncoder model.

function_skeletons.name: train
function_skeletons.signature: def train(model: nn.Module, train_loader: DataLoader, optimizer: Optimizer, criterion: nn.Module, epochs: int) -> None:
function_skeletons.docstring:
Train the MiniEncoder model on the training dataset.

Args:
    model (nn.Module): The MiniEncoder model to train.
    train_loader (DataLoader): DataLoader for the training dataset.
    optimizer (Optimizer): Optimizer for updating model weights.
    criterion (nn.Module): Loss function for training.
    epochs (int): Number of training epochs.
core_steps: Set the model to training mode.
Iterate over the number of epochs.
For each epoch, iterate over the training data.
Perform forward pass, compute loss, and backpropagate.
Update model weights using the optimizer.

acceptance_criteria: The training function runs without errors and updates model weights.
The model achieves a loss reduction over epochs.

files.purpose: Evaluation of the trained MiniEncoder model.

function_skeletons.name: evaluate
function_skeletons.signature: def evaluate(model: nn.Module, test_loader: DataLoader) -> Dict[str, float]:
function_skeletons.docstring:
Evaluate the MiniEncoder model on the test dataset.

Args:
    model (nn.Module): The trained MiniEncoder model.
    test_loader (DataLoader): DataLoader for the test dataset.

Returns:
    Dict[str, float]: A dictionary containing evaluation metrics such as accuracy and F1 score.
core_steps: Set the model to evaluation mode.
Iterate over the test data and collect predictions.
Compute evaluation metrics such as accuracy and F1 score.

acceptance_criteria: The evaluation function runs without errors and returns metrics in the expected format.
